text:
Maya: Uploaded a new tiny-first-run checklist mock — goal: reduce cognitive load on signup. Key change: replace full-width quickstart banner with a left-aligned checklist column and a right rail with 3 sample project cards (collapsed by default). Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/tiny-checklist (frame 'First Run / Checklist Rail'). Thoughts?

Omar: I like the left column for checklist tasks. Question: will users miss the sample cards when collapsed? Need a clear affordance.

Jess: We should experiment with a small animated pulse on the collapse chevron for first session only. Metric: sample_impression -> sample_start. 5k new users per arm.

Sam: Dev note: ensure the collapse control is a semantic button and appears early in DOM so screen readers and keyboarders find it. Also add data-qa attributes: data-qa="firstrun-samples-toggle" and data-qa="sample-cta".

Priya: Accessibility checklist: 1) contrast of chevron label is 3.6:1, needs 4.5:1; 2) collapsed state must have aria-expanded="false" on the button; 3) when samples expand, focus should move to the first sample CTA (use focus management).

Maya: Good calls. Microcopy: CTA copy options — "Try sample", "Use sample project", "Add example". Which is clearest?

Jess: "Use sample project" is explicit but long. For the rail maybe desktop gets full copy, mobile uses "Try sample". Also add a small "Why this?" link under the checklist explaining benefits.

Omar: Analytics: tag events sample_impression, sample_expand, sample_click, checklist_complete. Also record keyboard vs pointer.

Sam: Quick CSS hint to keep hit area large on mobile:
```
.firstrun-toggle { min-height:44px; padding: 10px 14px; }
.rail-cards { display:flex; gap:12px; overflow:hidden; }
```

Priya: a11y-bot: automated scan flagged missing aria-label on the "Why this?" icon. Recommend aria-describedby to link tooltip content.

Maya: I'll update the Figma: 1) increase chevron contrast and add pulse variant, 2) set CTA copy to "Use sample project" on desktop, "Try sample" on mobile, 3) add a11y notes (aria-expanded, aria-describedby, focus move), 4) annotate GA event names. Will post updated frames tomorrow morning.

Jess: After frames, I'll wire the GA experiment and share the tracking spec.

Omar: +1 to the pulse for first session only. Keep it subtle.

Maya: Thanks everyone — will follow up with the new export and a 10-minute keyboard review in #design-review.

Priya: Also request: please include the SR walkthrough steps in the Figma notes (how focus flows, expected announcements).
